gen-fs-kalam-space-grotesk: Hand-drawn and cozy, Kalam pulls its lines tight, while Space Grotesk, a sans-serif, draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width. Space Grotesk's drafting-pen steadiness is the standout, made for quick reads.
gen-fs-karma-fs-supreme: Karma sets a refined serif voice, its rounded lowercase forms standing tall and each s open enough to see through. Supreme then runs crisp across a paragraph, a heavy-looking strip of text whose letters stay held open.
gen-fs-karma-general-sans: Karma leads with comfortable serif forms, its hairlines present but never razor thin. And General Sans, a sans-serif with rod-stock horizontals and verticals, gives that refinement a clean, professional footing.
gen-fs-karma-satoshi: Comfortable and refined, Karma keeps its serif contrast tame, with tall rounded lowercase forms. But what stands out most is the gap between Karma's gentle weight shifts and Satoshi's uniform, wide-open strokes.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-fs-neco: Kohinoor Zerone draws round, wire-bent letters with contemporary precision, best left to just a few words. Neco swells gently from hairline to stem and handles the dignified, authoritative running text.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-fs-recia: Kohinoor Zerone draws round, precise letters like bent wire, with diagonals as hefty as its stems. And Recia's gentle modulation keeps openings generous, which suits a quick bit of reading.
gen-fs-merriweather-sans-fs-erode: Erode brings a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and descenders, and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight to the text. Merriweather Sans offers big, glassy counters; Erode offers dignified editorial text.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-hepta-slab: Locked together like links in a fine chain, New Title stands tall in its lowercase. And Hepta Slab, with open counters and curves and straights sharing one width, is the stretched-out partner to that tight chain.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-kiwi-maru: Letters locked together like links in a fine chain, and a lowercase that towers over the capitals, define New Title. Kiwi Maru, with ring-round o's and distant terminals, is the traditional counterweight.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-padyakke-expanded-on: Padyakke Expanded One spreads its glyphs like knots on a slack rope, with a pitcher-wide mouth in each c. Padyakke Expanded One keeps a constant pen-like line, while New Title locks its tall letters together.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Modern, New Title locks its tall lowercase together like chain links. Stint Ultra Expanded lets each character float apart, so extended reading moves at an unhurried pace, counters leading outward.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-fauna-one: Oswald packs its rows tight and speaks with confidence. Fauna One brings a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and descenders, and a generous entry into the e, all literary and dignified.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-glegoo: Oswald knits its rows tightly and speaks with confident strength, a display face with a moderate lowercase. Then Glegoo's big counters and tall lowercase give those rows somewhere refined and editorial to land.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-hanuman: Oswald packs its tall, confident letters into tightly knit rows, and Hanuman, a refined text serif, stands noticeably taller in the lowercase. Make the heading small and that strength fades fast.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-kadwa: Confident and strong, Oswald leads with narrow, tightly knit lines. Oswald is built to hit hard in a heading, while Kadwa, a serif with open-ended curves and a generous x-height, is built to settle into the text.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noticia-text: Tight and tall up top, literary below: Oswald stacks its rows close, while Noticia Text curls into each round letter with a big visible entrance. Dignity meets muscle.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-piazzolla: Oswald brings a confident, tightly knit heading with a firm, compact build. Piazzolla counters with a text serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, and whose e opens like a pried clasp.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-pridi: Pridi reads as a refined text serif, its small letters standing proud and almost capital-sized, with generous space between curve ends and the stem. Oswald's tight, strong rows make a firm heading above it.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-scope-one: Compact strength meets soft spill. Oswald sets tightly knit rows, strong and confident. Scope One, a classic serif with counters that spill into the surrounding space and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height, would read in a relaxed, traditional way over many lines.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-slabo-13px: Tightly knit rows give Oswald its confident, strong look, and the bookish Slabo 13px follows with large open counters in its tall a, e and s. And its rounded letters stay clearly open, a dignified foil.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-suwannaphum: Dignified and editorial, Suwannaphum has a high x-height like a squared-off woodblock letter. Across a full page, its text serif shapes, with a c as open as a bent paperclip, would feel sturdy and unhurried beside Oswald.
gen-fs-oswald-mulish: Oswald's most distinctive trait is its tightly knit rows, giving the heading a confident, strong look, while Mulish keeps a modern, approachable line with a large x-height. Over a long page, its sans would feel smooth and ruler-straight.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Paquito, a sturdy and warm serif whose lowercase fills the line like capitals, sits above a body whose heavy-looking strip of text would carry a long page steadily.
